new_elements: Door button + timer knob (Two parts); Twist-to-set door handle (Handle opens door; rotating it after closing winds the timer); Handle doubles as timer (One touchpoint)
rationale: The hand is already on the handle; no search for controls.
judge_comment: Merging the door handle and timer into a single touchpoint is intuitive and feasible, though the twist-to-set mapping still needs some learning.

title: Plug-in replaces power switch
new_elements: Standby electronics / clock to set (Flashing 12:00 syndrome); Pure mechanical, no clock (No display, no standby; nothing to configure on plug-in); Zero setup (Works out of the box)
rationale: The first interaction is already cooking, not configuring.
judge_comment: Removing the clock and standby electronics cuts setup, but it only partly addresses how cooking itself is operated, and the mechanism is vague.

title: Sliding glass front, no latch
new_elements: Push-release latch (Needs force and knowledge); Garage-style roll-up shutter (Metal shutter slides up; closing it completes the RF seal and starts); Shutter open/close (One sweeping motion)
rationale: No hidden button; the opening is the control.
judge_comment: A roll-up shutter that closes and starts the cycle makes operation intuitive, but sealing RF with a sliding shutter is hard and the cook time is unspecified.

title: Temperature-strip on turntable rim
new_elements: Lamp for visual checking (Shows food, not heat); Liquid-crystal thermometer strip (Aquarium-style strip on turntable edge reads plate temperature); Read temperature at a glance (Passive, cheap)
rationale: Removes guesswork about whether food is hot enough.
judge_comment: A strip is simple and passive, but it measures plate temperature rather than food, and it does little for operating the oven.

title: Spring-loaded 'squeeze' timer
new_elements: Rotary clockwork (Twisting); Squeeze-bulb pneumatic timer (Squeeze a rubber bulb; air bleed-back runs the cycle); Grip strength = time (Instinctive)
rationale: Whole-hand gesture with immediate tactile feedback.
judge_comment: A squeeze-bulb pneumatic timer is wildly novel and intuitive, but its accuracy and its ability to drive the magnetron are doubtful.

title: Thermal-camera shows hot/cold spots
new_elements: Incandescent lamp + user poking food (Learned testing ritual); Low-res thermal sensor + door display (8x8 thermopile paints a heat map on door); See heat not light (Doneness is visible)
rationale: No experience needed to judge whether the middle is cold.
judge_comment: An 8x8 thermopile heat map on the door is plausible and makes doneness visible, but it adds complexity and does not simplify operation.

title: Reusable lid-as-program token
new_elements: Panel controls (Set per use); Coded silicone lids (Lids with magnet patterns; cavity reed switches read lid and run its program); Lid is the recipe (Cover the food, done)
rationale: Choosing a lid is already a step users take; now it's the only step.
judge_comment: Coded lids that select the program remove nearly all steps and are plausible with reed switches, though a lid-less or unsuitable container is an edge case.

title: Wall-socket style timer plug
new_elements: Integrated timer knob (Part of oven panel); Twist-timer on the plug (Oven has no controls; the mains plug has a classic wind-up timer; always full power); Timer on the cord (Oven body is just a box)
rationale: Oven itself has nothing to learn; the plug is a familiar timer.
judge_comment: A familiar wind-up timer on the plug is intuitive, but a plug timer switching high microwave loads and the awkward placement raise safety and usability concerns.

title: Light-pipe window replaces lamp
new_elements: Interior 25 W lamp (Burns out, dim); Roof light-pipe/skylight (Mesh-shielded acrylic pipe brings kitchen light into cavity); Passive illumination (Never fails)
rationale: Checking food always works; no bulb-replacement procedure to learn.
judge_comment: A passive light pipe is a reasonable substitution but barely affects operational simplicity, and a light pipe through a shielded cavity gives dim light.

title: Dial that reads back in seconds-remaining aloud
new_elements: Silent dial (Must be read); Talking knob chip (Greeting-card sound chip announces 'two minutes' as you turn); Spoken confirmation (Eyes-free setting)
rationale: Confirms intent instantly, so mistakes aren't discovered later.
judge_comment: A cheap sound chip confirming the setting helps a bit, but it adds a feature instead of substituting and is not radical.

title: Momentary dead-man heating
new_elements: Timer + bell + power knob (Set-and-forget complexity); Hold-to-heat paddle (Heats only while large paddle is held; release = stop; watch food through glass); Direct manual heating (Like a stove knob but instant)
rationale: Cause and effect are immediate and continuous; nothing to pre-plan.
judge_comment: A hold-to-heat paddle needs no learning and gives immediate cause and effect, but holding it for minutes is tiresome and the safety interlock design is a challenge.

title: Food-pictogram dial replaces power knob
new_elements: Pictogram food dial (Single knob with icons (mug, plate, frozen block, popcorn) that maps directly to a fixed power/time pair.)
rationale: Users pick what they are heating rather than translating it into watts and minutes.
judge_comment: Intuitive and cheap, but food-icon presets already exist on many microwaves, so it is not radical.

title: Weighing turntable replaces timer knob
new_elements: Load-cell turntable hub (Turntable spindle sits on a strain gauge; mass sets cooking time automatically.); Derives cook time from food mass (Time = k × weight, no user input.)
rationale: Nothing to set: put food in, close the door, it knows how long.
judge_comment: Weight-based auto-time removes input, but mass alone is a poor predictor of cook time across food types, and the load cell adds cost.

title: IR 'hot enough' sensor replaces the timer entirely
new_elements: Non-contact IR food thermometer (Thermopile in cavity ceiling stops the magnetron when the food surface reaches eating temperature.); Cooks to temperature not time (Single 'Heat' button, auto-stop.)
rationale: Replaces a guessing-game knob with one button that always yields hot food.
judge_comment: A one-button heat-to-temperature design fits the need well, though IR only reads surface temperature and steam and containers can interfere.

title: Magnetic soft-close door replaces push-button latch
new_elements: Magnetic door retention (Rare-earth magnets hold the door; pull anywhere on its edge to open, no button, no hooks.)
rationale: Opens like a fridge, which every user already knows how to use.
judge_comment: A fridge-style door is familiar and easy to use, but it is a minor part of operation and the magnets must still work with the safety interlocks.

title: Hall-effect door sensors replace interlock microswitches
new_elements: Redundant Hall-effect door sensors (Solid-state magnet sensors with cross-check logic; no mechanical wear, door closes with any gentle push.)
rationale: No 'slam it harder' learning curve because closure detection no longer depends on switch travel.
judge_comment: A sound technical swap that makes door closing more forgiving, but it barely affects the overall learning curve.

title: Mode stirrer replaces turntable and its motor
new_elements: Fan-driven waveguide mode stirrer (Rotating metal paddle in the waveguide spreads energy; cavity has a flat ceramic floor.)
rationale: Removes the misaligned-plate / off-the-roller failure that confuses first-time users.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are real and plausible, but they only weakly serve no-learning-curve operation, since the plate-misalignment problem is minor.

title: Three-detent 'Defrost / Reheat / Cook' knob replaces 5-step cam
new_elements: Three-position power selector (Cam with only three heavy detents and plain words, no percentages.)
rationale: Fewer, named choices eliminate decision paralysis.
judge_comment: Plain-word detents directly cut complexity and are easy to build, though the idea is incremental.

title: Speech chip replaces the mechanical bell
new_elements: Voice announcement module (Says 'Your food is ready – careful, it is hot' instead of ringing.)
rationale: Plain-language feedback needs no interpretation of beeps.
judge_comment: Voice feedback is clear and cheap, but it is common and does not affect operating the controls.

title: Door handle twist sets time
new_elements: Rotary door handle timer (The grab handle is the clockwork timer; twist it as you close the door.)
rationale: Closing and setting become one gesture on one part.
judge_comment: Merging door closing and time setting into one gesture is intuitive and novel, but the door-handle mechanics and safety interlocks are tricky.

title: Docking plate replaces power cord
new_elements: Contact docking base (Oven sits on a powered base plate with spring contacts; no cord to route or plug.)
rationale: Set-up is 'put it down', with no cable management.
judge_comment: A cordless docking base is a novel idea, but it adds cost and power-transfer challenges and barely touches operating simplicity.

title: Glass-ceramic waveguide window replaces mica
new_elements: Wipe-clean glass-ceramic RF window (Non-porous ceramic that never delaminates or scorches, so no replacement instructions exist.)
rationale: Removes a maintenance task the user would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: Plausible swap for the mica cover, but it addresses maintenance rather than operation, so it barely serves the no-learning-curve need.

title: Silicone mat replaces glass turntable
new_elements: Flexible silicone cavity mat (Unbreakable, dishwasher-safe, drops in any orientation.)
rationale: No fragile plate to break or re-seat on a roller ring.
judge_comment: A silicone mat in the cavity is easy to handle, but it is not about operation, and heat tolerance and uneven heating without rotation are concerns.

title: Inverter supply replaces duty-cycle cam
new_elements: Inverter magnetron drive (Continuous true power control; 'low' means gentle, not on-off pulsing.)
rationale: The knob behaves like a stove flame, matching users' existing mental model.
judge_comment: Inverter power control already exists in some models, and it makes power levels intuitive and predictable like a stove flame.

title: Tap-to-add button replaces timer dial
new_elements: Single +30 s tap button (Each tap adds 30 seconds and starts immediately.)
rationale: Counting taps is simpler than reading a dial scale.
judge_comment: A +30 s button is simple and already common, so the idea is practical but not radical.

title: Single push-twist knob replaces both knobs
new_elements: Combined push-depth / twist control (Twist sets minutes, push depth sets power (shallow = defrost, deep = full).)
rationale: One control, one hand, no sequence to remember.
judge_comment: A single control is appealing, but push-depth for power is hard to discover and imprecise, so it may add learning.

title: Food probe replaces timer
new_elements: Shielded cavity temperature probe (Stick into food, dial a target temperature; magnetron stops at target.)
rationale: 'How hot' is a more intuitive question than 'how many minutes at what percent'.
judge_comment: Probe with target temperature is intuitive but already exists in some ovens, needs user to insert probe, and metal in cavity is tricky.

title: Humidity sensor auto-stop replaces timer
new_elements: Exhaust steam sensor (Detects steam burst from food and ends the cycle a set delay later.)
rationale: Reheating becomes a single 'go' with no numeric input.
judge_comment: Single-press auto-stop strongly removes the learning curve, though sensor cooking is already on the market.

title: Solid-state GaN RF source replaces HV chain
new_elements: Low-voltage solid-state RF generator (Transistor amplifier at ~50 V replaces magnetron, transformer, diode and HV capacitor.)
rationale: Accurate, instant power lets controls say exactly what they do, with no warm-up quirks to learn.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is real and radical, but the link to simple operation is indirect and cost is high.

title: PTC thermistor replaces bimetal thermostat
new_elements: Self-resetting PTC overheat limiter (Resistive element throttles current when hot; no manual reset button.)
rationale: Users never meet a 'why did it stop working' reset procedure.
judge_comment: Plausible swap that removes a rare reset annoyance but barely touches everyday operation.

title: Transparent conductive film replaces perforated door screen
new_elements: ITO-coated glass RF shield (Optically clear conductive coating blocks microwaves without a mesh.)
rationale: Users see boil-over coming without peering through a dark grid.
judge_comment: Clear door aids visibility, but it doesn't simplify operation much and the shielding at microwave frequencies is challenging.

title: Edge-lit LED ceiling replaces incandescent lamp
new_elements: LED edge-lit cavity ceiling panel (Even, cool light that also flashes to signal 'done'.)
rationale: Bright view and visual status in one part, no bulb to change.
judge_comment: Practical LED swap with a done-flash cue, but only marginally reduces the learning curve and is not radical.

title: Absorbing ferrite gasket replaces quarter-wave choke
new_elements: Ferrite-loaded elastomer door gasket (Absorbs leakage so door alignment tolerances are relaxed.)
rationale: Door seals with any casual push, removing the 'is it really closed?' doubt.
judge_comment: Ferrite gasket is plausible and could ease door closing, but the link to operational simplicity is indirect and safety certification is demanding.

title: Foot pedal replaces door button
new_elements: Toe-kick door release pedal (Kick plate under the oven pops the door while hands hold the dish.)
rationale: Hands-full operation is the real-world default; no juggling needed.
judge_comment: A toe-kick door release is intuitive and handy with full hands, though it covers only door opening rather than overall operation.

title: Voice command replaces knobs
new_elements: Offline keyword voice controller ('Two minutes', 'defrost', 'stop' – local recognition, no app.)
rationale: Speaking the intent is the lowest possible learning curve.
judge_comment: Offline keyword voice control directly removes the learning curve and is feasible, though not entirely new.

title: NFC packaging reader replaces controls
new_elements: Door-frame NFC reader (Reads cooking instructions encoded on ready-meal tags and runs them.)
rationale: Tap the box, press go – the package knows better than the user.
judge_comment: Tap-to-cook via NFC on packaging is near-zero learning, but it depends on package adoption and does not cover non-tagged food.

title: Camera food recognition replaces knobs and window
new_elements: Cavity camera with food classifier (Identifies dish type and volume, sets program, streams view to front display.)
rationale: Zero settings: the oven looks at the food and decides.
judge_comment: Zero-setting operation fits the need perfectly, but camera food recognition is costly and not a cheaper substitution, and similar ideas already exist in smart ovens.

title: Toaster-style pop-open door replaces bell
new_elements: Timer-released door spring (At zero the clockwork trips the latch; door swings ajar as the 'done' signal.)
rationale: Done-state is unmistakable and food is already accessible.
judge_comment: A toaster-style pop-open door gives an intuitive done signal and is simple and plausible, though it only addresses the end of the interaction.

title: Door hinge as the only interlock switch
new_elements: Conductive hinge-pin contact (The hinge itself completes the control circuit only at full-closed angle.)
rationale: Fewer hidden parts to misalign means the door 'just works'.
judge_comment: Using the hinge as the interlock is a clever simplification, but users never see it, so it barely helps learning, and safety-critical interlocks need redundancy.

title: Three preset buttons replace 0-30 min dial
new_elements: Three fixed-duration mechanical buttons (1 min / 3 min / 6 min spring buttons, each a separate clockwork.)
rationale: No scale to read; pick short, medium or long.
judge_comment: Three presets remove the need to read a scale and are easy to build, but the idea is incremental and inflexible.

title: Slot-in recipe cards replace knobs
new_elements: Punched recipe card reader (Physical card with notches sets time and power when inserted; cards ship with the oven.)
rationale: Tangible, labelled cards replace abstract settings.
judge_comment: Notched recipe cards make settings tangible and are inventive, but they add loose parts that can be lost and mean the user has to choose a card.

title: Embossed tactile shapes replace printed scales
new_elements: Tactile-shape control fascia (Raised cup, plate and snowflake shapes locatable by touch.)
rationale: Usable without reading, glasses or good lighting.
judge_comment: Tactile shapes make controls easy to find without reading, but this is a modest, fairly obvious change and does not by itself make operation intuitive.

title: Light-ring touch dial replaces clockwork timer
new_elements: Capacitive LED ring timer (Swipe around a ring of lights; lit arc shows remaining time, precise to the second.)
rationale: Time is shown as a shrinking arc, which needs no numeracy.
judge_comment: A swipe ring with a shrinking arc is intuitive and plausible, though it resembles existing touch dials and swiping may not be obvious to every user.

title: Hand crank replaces timer knob
new_elements: Wind-up crank timer (One full crank turn equals one minute; stored spring energy also drives the turntable.)
rationale: Counting cranks is physical and obvious; also removes a motor.
judge_comment: A wind-up crank is physical and radical, but a spring driving the turntable is questionable and cranking adds effort and a possible accuracy problem.

title: Pull-out drawer replaces turntable and swing door
new_elements: Sliding cavity drawer (Food tray slides out toward the user like a kitchen drawer; closing starts cooking.)
rationale: Loading, closing and starting collapse into one familiar push.
judge_comment: A drawer that starts cooking on close is very simple to use, but microwave sealing, safety interlocks and spilled liquids make it hard to build.

title: Drop-down oven door replaces side-hinged door
new_elements: Bottom-hinged shelf door (Door folds down to form a landing shelf for hot dishes.)
rationale: Mirrors a conventional oven so users transfer existing habits.
judge_comment: A drop-down door borrows familiar oven habits and is feasible, but it is already used on some compact ovens and only partly helps simplicity.

title: Colour-wedge timer scale replaces minute numbers
new_elements: Colour-zoned timer bezel (Dial face divided into blue (drink), green (plate), red (frozen) zones instead of minutes.)
rationale: Turn to the colour that matches your food; no arithmetic.
judge_comment: Colour zones remove arithmetic and are easy to build, but they are imprecise and not very radical.

title: Neon charge indicator replaces hidden bleed resistor
new_elements: Visible HV discharge neon lamp (Lamp across the capacitor glows until the charge is safely bled off.)
rationale: Safety state is self-explanatory: light on means wait.
judge_comment: A neon discharge lamp is plausible but concerns servicing and safety, not user operation, so it barely serves the need.

title: Colour-changing handle replaces bell
new_elements: Thermochromic illuminated handle (Glows amber while cooking, green when done, red if contents are very hot.)
rationale: Status is read at a glance from across the room, silently.
judge_comment: A glanceable status handle is intuitive, but a thermochromic handle that signals food temperature is hard to build and doesn't simplify operation.

title: Hand-wave sensor replaces door button
new_elements: IR proximity door opener (Wave a hand in front of the door and a solenoid releases the latch.)
rationale: No button to find or force; gesture is self-evident.
judge_comment: Wave-to-open is intuitive and feasible with an IR sensor and solenoid, though a door button is already simple and accidental triggering is possible.

title: Optical beam interlock replaces monitor switch
new_elements: Through-beam optical door sensor (Door tab breaks an IR beam; non-contact so closing force is irrelevant.)
rationale: Door closes softly and reliably every time, no slamming technique required.
judge_comment: A non-contact door sensor helps soft closing, but safety interlocks need redundancy and the user benefit is marginal.

title: Metallised polymer cavity replaces steel box
new_elements: Vacuum-metallised moulded cavity (Lightweight plastic shell with aluminium coating forms the RF enclosure.)
rationale: A few-kilogram oven can be carried and placed anywhere by a student with no installation.
judge_comment: A lightweight metallised plastic cavity is interesting, but it serves portability rather than simple operation, and RF containment, heat resistance and safety are doubtful.

title: Hand-rotated turntable sets the timer
new_elements: Turntable-as-timer spindle (Rotate the plate by hand to wind the clockwork; it unwinds while rotating the food.)
rationale: The thing you already touch when loading food is the only control.
judge_comment: Using the turntable as a clockwork timer is a clever, intuitive single control, though winding the plate and getting accurate timing are tricky.

title: Phone buzz replaces bell
new_elements: Bluetooth done-notifier (Sends a single 'ready' notification; no app set-up beyond pairing.)
rationale: Alert reaches the user wherever they are without any ongoing interaction.
judge_comment: A phone notification is easy to build but adds pairing and dependence on a phone, which does little for no-learning-curve operation.

title: Mug cradle replaces time/power settings for drinks
new_elements: Dedicated mug cradle with switch (Placing a mug in the cradle triggers a fixed gentle-heat beverage cycle with stir pause.)
rationale: The most common task needs zero settings and avoids superheating.
judge_comment: A mug cradle that starts a fixed beverage cycle removes settings for the most common task and is plausible with sensing, but it covers a narrow use case.

title: Pull-cord timer replaces knob
new_elements: Retracting pull-cord clockwork (Pull the cord out to a length marked with food icons; release to start.)
rationale: Length is a more intuitive quantity than dial angle.
judge_comment: A pull-cord with food-icon markings is simple and intuitive, but it is only a modest change from a dial and has some mechanical wear and accuracy limits.

title: One-button 'Reheat' oven
new_elements: Single-program reheat button (Only control: a big button running a sensor-terminated reheat cycle.)
rationale: A product with one button cannot be operated wrongly.
judge_comment: Directly delivers zero learning curve, but single-button microwaves are not very novel and the sensor-terminated cycle is lightly specified.

title: Airflow-spun floor replaces turntable motor
new_elements: Fan-exhaust driven turbine platter (Magnetron cooling air turns a vaned platter; no separate motor.)
rationale: Fewer parts to fail means fewer error states the user must understand.
judge_comment: A clever part substitution, but it barely affects the user's operation, and the airflow is unlikely to turn a loaded platter reliably.

title: Sliding door replaces hinged door and latch
new_elements: Side-sliding RF door (Door slides on rails into the housing; no swing clearance or button.)
rationale: Works in tight dorm spaces with an obvious slide gesture.
judge_comment: The slide gesture is intuitive and the door saves space, but RF sealing on a sliding door is difficult and the benefit to operation is modest.

title: Metal-detect coil replaces warning labels
new_elements: Cavity metal-detection coil (Inductive sensor refuses to start and lights an icon when metal is inside.)
rationale: Users need not learn the no-metal rule; the oven enforces it.
judge_comment: The oven enforces the no-metal rule so users need not learn it, and inductive metal sensing is plausible, though small metal items and metal-trimmed dishes may cause detection errors.

title: Fully transparent cavity shell replaces lamp and window
new_elements: Transparent conductive-mesh glass enclosure (Whole cavity made of laminated glass with embedded fine mesh; ambient light suffices.)
rationale: Everything is visible from any angle so mistakes are caught without instruction.
judge_comment: A radical idea, but a laminated glass cavity with mesh would be costly and hard to build, and visibility only loosely supports ease of operation.

title: Steam-sensor auto-stop replaces timer
new_elements: Exhaust humidity sensor (Detects steam burst from food and ends heating automatically.); Heats until food is done without user timing (No minutes to set.)
rationale: User presses one button and the oven decides when to stop, removing the timer entirely.
judge_comment: Directly removes the timer decision and is plausible, but humidity-sensor auto-cook already exists in many microwaves.

title: Weighing turntable sets time and power
new_elements: Load-cell turntable hub (Weighs the dish and derives duration and power automatically.)
rationale: Weight replaces two knobs with zero decisions.
judge_comment: Weight-based auto settings reduce inputs, but weight alone poorly determines the right time and power for different foods.

title: Mode stirrer replaces turntable
new_elements: Rotating metal stirrer fan in waveguide (Spreads RF pattern so food heats evenly on a fixed flat floor.)
rationale: No plate to misplace, break or trip on; just put food anywhere.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are standard in existing microwaves, and removing the turntable adds little to ease of operation.

title: Solid-state frequency-sweep RF replaces turntable motor
new_elements: LDMOS solid-state microwave generator (Low-voltage transistor RF source sweeps frequency for uniform heating.)
rationale: No moving parts and no lethal HV, food just heats evenly wherever placed.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF is a genuinely radical substitution, but it is expensive and only tangentially related to the no-learning-curve need.

title: Magnetic door catch replaces push-button latch
new_elements: Magnetic door catch (Fridge-style magnet strip holds door; user just pulls handle.)
rationale: Opening works like every fridge the user already knows.
judge_comment: Familiar fridge-style opening is simple, but a magnetic catch is unlikely to meet microwave door-safety interlock needs and is a minor change.

title: Hall-effect door sensors replace microswitches
new_elements: Redundant Hall-effect magnetic sensing (Contactless sensors detect door magnet; no wear, no misalignment.)
rationale: Door never 'fails to register', avoiding confusing non-starts.
judge_comment: Reliable and plausible, but it's an incremental internal component swap with only a weak link to user learning curve.

title: Optical light-curtain interlock
new_elements: Infrared beam-break door sensor (IR beam across door frame interrupted only when door fully shut.)
rationale: Removes the 'slam it harder' learning step of stiff microswitches.
judge_comment: Beam-break sensing is feasible and removes a minor annoyance, but needs a safety-rated redundant interlock and barely affects ease of operation.

title: Low-voltage inverter replaces HV doubler
new_elements: Resonant switch-mode inverter supply (Generates magnetron voltage without a large storage capacitor.)
rationale: Continuous power means settings behave intuitively instead of pulsing.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist and give continuous power, but the user-facing benefit to simplicity is indirect.

title: PTC thermistor replaces bimetal thermostat
new_elements: Self-resetting PTC thermal limiter (Resistance spikes with heat, throttling the magnetron without snapping contacts.)
rationale: Invisible protection that never leaves the user wondering why it stopped.
judge_comment: Invisible protection has little bearing on operation, and PTC throttling of a magnetron is questionable.

title: Single 'add 30 s' button replaces timer dial
new_elements: One large +30 s start button (Each press adds 30 s and starts immediately; nothing else.)
rationale: One button, one rule; counting presses is the whole interface.
judge_comment: Directly delivers zero-learning-curve operation with a single button, though it limits control and the concept is somewhat familiar.

title: Food-icon dial replaces minutes
new_elements: Pictogram selector dial (Positions show mug, plate, soup, popcorn; each maps to preset time and power.)
rationale: User chooses what they have, not how long to cook it.
judge_comment: Highly intuitive pictogram selection that removes time and power decisions, though similar preset dials already exist.

title: NFC package reader replaces controls
new_elements: NFC food-package tag reading (Antenna under cavity floor reads cooking programme from packaging tag.)
rationale: Zero settings: the meal tells the oven what to do.
judge_comment: Zero-setting operation is ideal, but it depends on packaging tags that are not standardised and does not work for non-packaged food.

title: Delete the power knob: fixed full power
new_elements: Single fixed-power design (timer only) (Power knob and duty-cycle cam removed; only duration remains.)
rationale: One knob fewer means one concept fewer to learn.
judge_comment: Removing power control simplifies the interface and is cheap, but it hurts cooking quality for defrosting and delicate foods.

title: Inductive power pad replaces mains cord
new_elements: High-power inductive countertop coupling (Oven sits on a flush counter coil; no cord, no plug.)
rationale: Place it and it works; no cable routing or sockets.
judge_comment: Wireless power is radical, but it barely affects the learning curve of operating the oven and kilowatt-class inductive coupling is impractical.

title: Auto-opening door replaces end bell
new_elements: Spring door pop-open at timer end (Timer trips the latch so the door swings open as the done signal.)
rationale: The open door is an unmistakable, language-free 'ready'.
judge_comment: A pop-open door is a clear language-free done signal and mechanically simple, but it is only a minor part of operation and could be a nuisance or hazard.

title: Glass-ceramic waveguide window replaces mica
new_elements: Glass-ceramic (LAS) waveguide cover (Wipe-clean non-absorbent cover that cannot char or arc.)
rationale: No maintenance knowledge needed about replacing scorched mica.
judge_comment: Reduces maintenance burden but barely touches operational simplicity, and glass-ceramic covers are already used in some designs.

title: Silicone mat replaces glass turntable
new_elements: Flexible silicone cavity mat (Unbreakable, non-slip, dishwasher-safe floor in place of glass plate and roller ring.)
rationale: Nothing to seat correctly or shatter; cleaning is intuitive.
judge_comment: Removes turntable seating but loses rotation for even heating and silicone heat and arcing behavior is a concern; modest link to operation.

title: Conductive elastomer gasket replaces choke seal
new_elements: Conductive silicone RF gasket (Compressible metallised rubber seals RF regardless of door alignment.)
rationale: Door seals even when closed casually, removing precision-closing habits.
judge_comment: Conductive gaskets exist and forgiving door closure is plausible, but the benefit to operation is minor.

title: Pull-out drawer replaces hinged door
new_elements: Drawer-style cavity (Whole floor slides out like a kitchen drawer; pushing it in closes the interlock.)
rationale: Loading a drawer is a universally understood gesture.
judge_comment: Intuitive drawer gesture is appealing, but sealing a large sliding RF cavity and spill containment are hard.

title: IR food thermometer replaces timer
new_elements: Infrared surface thermometer (Stops heating when food reaches target temperature chosen on a 'warm/hot/boil' dial.); Heats to a target temperature (Outcome-based control.)
rationale: Users think in 'hot enough', not minutes.
judge_comment: Outcome-based warm/hot/boil control directly removes the need to know times, though IR measures only surface temperature and some sensor-cooking exists already.

title: Continuous inverter power replaces duty-cycle cam
new_elements: Variable-amplitude inverter power control (True 10-100% output instead of on/off pulsing.)
rationale: Power knob behaves like a stove dial, matching existing mental models.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist, and a stove-like power dial helps only partly since the user still has to set a time.

title: Tap-the-top to start one minute
new_elements: Piezo tap sensor in casing (Each tap on the lid adds one minute and starts heating.)
rationale: No panel at all; the oven itself is the button.
judge_comment: A tap-to-add-a-minute interface is very simple and cheap to build, though it may trigger accidentally and the tap-to-stop behavior is unclear.

title: Foot pedal start
new_elements: Hold-to-heat foot pedal (Heats only while pedal is pressed; release stops.)
rationale: Direct hands-free control with no timing concept to learn.
judge_comment: Hold-to-heat has no timing to learn, but it is awkward and a safety and ergonomics concern for long heating.

title: Plain-word slider replaces power percentages
new_elements: Linear slider labelled defrost / warm / reheat / boil (Words replace wattage or percentage steps.)
rationale: Intent-named positions need no manual.
judge_comment: Intent-labelled positions are intuitive and trivially cheap, but the idea is incremental and still leaves time to set.

title: Camera doneness vision replaces timer
new_elements: Embedded camera with on-device doneness model (Watches bubbling, steam and colour to stop heating.)
rationale: Single 'go' button; the oven watches so the user needn't.
judge_comment: A one-button oven that judges doneness itself removes the learning curve entirely, though reliable doneness detection through steam and a camera lens in a microwave is hard and costly.

title: Vibrating floor replaces rotating turntable
new_elements: Piezo-vibrated cavity floor (Micro-vibrations shuffle food slightly for even heating without rotation.)
rationale: Rectangular dishes fit anywhere; no 'will it spin' guesswork.
judge_comment: Piezo vibration of a cavity floor is unlikely to move food enough for even heating, and it only loosely serves ease of use, though it is a novel substitute for the turntable.

title: LED array replaces incandescent lamp
new_elements: Cool-white LED interior strip (Low-power lamp also colour-shifts to show heating / done state.)
rationale: Status shown by light colour, no display to read.
judge_comment: LED lamps are easy and cheap, and color-coded status helps a bit, but replacing the bulb is an obvious swap and the colors need some interpretation.

title: Door itself is the power contactor
new_elements: Door-hinge contact as mains interrupter (Closing the door physically bridges the magnetron primary circuit.)
rationale: Closed door equals on, open door equals off: the simplest possible rule.
judge_comment: Close-to-start is very intuitive, but using the door as the mains contactor is unsafe and would breach interlock safety rules, and there is no way to set a duration.

title: Colour-glow finish indicator replaces bell
new_elements: Edge-lit casing that glows green when done (Silent visual completion signal visible across the room.)
rationale: Universal colour code, no beep patterns to decode.
judge_comment: A glowing completion cue is simple and feasible and replaces the beep, but it only addresses the end signal, not operation.

title: Pull-cord winds the timer
new_elements: Pull-cord clockwork winder (Length of pull sets duration; let go to start.)
rationale: Physical, playful, obvious: longer pull equals longer heat.
judge_comment: A pull-cord timer is a physical, self-explanatory input that replaces the keypad, and it is feasible with a clockwork mechanism, though precision is limited.

title: Shape-coded buttons: mug and plate
new_elements: Two moulded buttons shaped as a mug and a plate (Each triggers a fixed preset for drinks or meals.)
rationale: Match the button to the object in your hand.
judge_comment: Directly removes the need to learn settings by matching buttons to objects, though it is a modest and limited substitution for a standard keypad.

title: Transparent conductive film replaces mesh window
new_elements: ITO / silver-nanowire RF-shielding glass coating (Clear door glass that blocks microwaves without perforated metal.)
rationale: Clear view means users check food naturally instead of reading timers.
judge_comment: A plausible, concrete component swap, but the link to no-learning-curve operation is weak, and RF shielding at microwave power with transparent films is challenging.

title: Auto-grounding relay replaces bleeder resistor
new_elements: Normally-closed HV shorting relay (Capacitor shorted to ground whenever mains is absent.)
rationale: Safe by default so nothing about the device needs to be understood.
judge_comment: A feasible safety component swap that the user never sees, so it does nothing for ease of operation.

title: Metallised polymer shell replaces steel casing
new_elements: Injection-moulded polymer with vacuum-metallised interior (Lightweight one-piece body with integrated controls.)
rationale: Light enough for a student to move and position without help.
judge_comment: Metallised polymer faces heat, arcing and shielding durability problems, and weight has little to do with operational simplicity.

title: Roller-shutter door replaces hinged door
new_elements: Vertical metal roller shutter with RF gasket (Shutter rolls up into the top; closes by pulling a tab down.)
rationale: No swing clearance, no latch button: pull down, done.
judge_comment: Pull-down shutter is an intuitive, radical door substitute, but RF sealing and hygiene with a roller mechanism are very difficult.

title: Rotating cavity replaces turntable
new_elements: Whole-cavity slow rotation drum (The sealed cavity rotates around the fixed waveguide.)
rationale: Floor is flat and fixed from the user's view; nothing to align.
judge_comment: Radical, but a rotating sealed cavity is complex and costly, and the turntable is not a real learning-curve problem.

title: Thermal fuse replaces thermostat
new_elements: One-shot thermal fuse (Cheap fusible link cuts power permanently on overheat.)
rationale: Cheaper protection with zero user interaction.
judge_comment: Cheap and plausible, but it is invisible to the user and does little for ease of operation; thermal fuses are already used in microwaves.

title: Frozen-or-not IR sensor replaces defrost setting
new_elements: Start-temperature IR probe (Detects frozen food and automatically selects defrost duty cycle.)
rationale: Defrost happens without the user knowing the word.
judge_comment: Auto-detecting frozen food removes a confusing setting, though it adds a sensor rather than a cheaper substitute.

title: Mug-only micro-microwave
new_elements: Mug-sized cavity with single preset (Cavity fits one mug; one button heats to drinking temperature.)
rationale: Removing options removes learning; perfect for a dorm.
judge_comment: A single-preset mug cavity eliminates choices and is easy to build, though it is limited in what it can heat.

title: 0-5 minute large dial replaces 0-30 min timer
new_elements: Short-range high-resolution timer dial (Full rotation spans 5 minutes with 10 s marks.)
rationale: Everyday reheats become precise with the same one-knob gesture.
judge_comment: A simple dial change that is easy to use and very feasible, but it only modestly reduces the learning curve.

title: Quartz synchronous timer replaces clockwork
new_elements: Synchronous-motor timer with cam (Mains-synchronised motor drives the dial back accurately.)
rationale: Keeps the trusted knob but makes short times behave as expected.
judge_comment: A synchronous motor timer is plausible and fixes short-time accuracy, but it's an incremental change that only slightly reduces the learning curve.

title: Latchless soft-close door
new_elements: Damped friction hinge door (Door stays shut by hinge friction and gasket compression; no hooks or button.)
rationale: Push to close, pull to open: no mechanism to discover.
judge_comment: A latchless door is simple to use, but it is a safety problem because microwave interlocks must be positive and redundant, so friction alone is unlikely to be compliant.

title: USB-C PD low-power microwave
new_elements: 240 W USB-C powered mini oven (Runs from a laptop charger; longer but plug-anywhere heating.)
rationale: Uses the one cable students already own.
judge_comment: A USB-C microwave is wild and familiar to use, but 240 W is too little for useful heating, and the magnetron needs high voltage, so it only partly serves the need.

title: Two-position power switch replaces 5-step knob
new_elements: Defrost / Full toggle switch (Only two states, clearly labelled.)
rationale: Binary choice is instantly understood.
judge_comment: A binary Defrost/Full switch is trivially understood and easy to build, though it is not radical and limits control.

title: Capacitive door-closure sensing
new_elements: Capacitive proximity door detection (Electrode in frame senses door metal flush against it.)
rationale: Door registers closed without force or clicks.
judge_comment: Capacitive door sensing is invisible to the user, but it has little effect on the learning curve and is a safety risk as the sole interlock.

title: Heated ceramic crisp floor replaces glass plate
new_elements: Ferrite-loaded ceramic crisping floor (Absorbs microwaves to get hot and browns food bottoms.)
rationale: Crisping happens automatically with no extra mode.
judge_comment: Susceptor-style crisping floors exist already; it removes a mode but only marginally helps the no-learning-curve need.

title: 48 V DC bus replaces HV transformer and diode
new_elements: Low-voltage DC distribution to RF amplifiers (Everything inside runs under 60 V; no HV section at all.)
rationale: Removes hidden hazards so the product can be as casual as a toaster.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF amplifiers at low voltage are plausible but not cheap, and the link to ease of operation is indirect.

title: Tactile detent knob replaces printed scale
new_elements: Knob with raised bumps per minute and braille (Settings felt, not read.)
rationale: Operable without looking or reading, in any language.
judge_comment: Tactile, language-free knob directly aids simple use and is easy to build, though not very radical.

title: Air-turbine turntable driven by cooling fan
new_elements: Fan-airflow-driven turntable hub (Magnetron cooling air spins a small turbine coupled to the plate; no separate motor.)
rationale: Cheaper and quieter with no change to how the user loads food.
judge_comment: Clever motor-removal substitution that cuts cost, but the user sees no change in operation.

title: Top-loading lid replaces front door
new_elements: Hinged top lid with gravity RF seal (Lid drops shut under its own weight and compresses the choke gasket.)
rationale: Lift lid, drop food in, close: the pot-and-lid gesture everyone knows.
judge_comment: Familiar pot-lid gesture makes use intuitive, though gravity RF sealing and spill handling are challenging.

title: Food-icon dial replaces time+power knobs
new_elements: Single pictogram dial (mug, bowl, plate, pizza, defrost) (One knob whose detents encode preset time/power pairs; no numbers at all.)
rationale: User picks a picture of what they are heating instead of reasoning about minutes and watts.
judge_comment: Pictogram presets are intuitive and easy to build, but similar auto-cook dials already exist, so novelty is low.

title: One big GO button with weight-sensing floor
new_elements: Load-cell cavity floor + single start button (Mass of the dish sets heating time; one button does everything.); Strain-gauge load cell (Low-cost weighing element under the turntable bearing.)
rationale: Zero settings: put food in, press GO.
judge_comment: One-button operation is ideal for no learning curve, but mass alone is a poor proxy for heating time, and a load cell on a rotating turntable is difficult to implement.

title: Hold-to-heat paddle (tap-style control)
new_elements: Spring-return heating paddle (Magnetron runs only while the big paddle is pressed, like a water tap.)
rationale: Short reheats need no timer at all; letting go stops it, which everyone already understands from taps.
judge_comment: A hold-to-run paddle is instantly understood and simple to build, though it is tiring for longer cooks and needs safety interlocks.

title: Pull-string timer like a wind-up toy
new_elements: Pull-cord clockwork timer (Pull the cord out to the distance you want; it reels back in as it cooks and stops at zero.)
rationale: A visible, physical remaining-time cue that children's toys already taught everyone.
judge_comment: A pull-cord clockwork timer is a tactile, visible and cheap mechanical substitute, but setting time precisely by distance is fiddly.

title: Hourglass sand timer with photo-gate cut-off
new_elements: Flip-hourglass start/stop (Flipping the glass starts the magnetron; an optical gate switches off when the sand runs out.)
rationale: The most universally understood timer in history; remaining time is read at a glance.
judge_comment: A flip hourglass is charming and universally understood, but it offers only fixed durations, and sand sensing adds complexity and gives little flexibility.

title: Target-temperature knob via IR sensor
new_elements: Infrared food thermometer + 'warm/hot/boiling' knob (User sets desired food temperature; oven stops when surface IR reaches it.); Thermopile IR sensing (Non-contact surface temperature readout through a mica window.)
rationale: People know how hot they want their food; they don't know watts and minutes.
judge_comment: A temperature knob matches how people think about food, though IR reads only the surface and the substitution is more of an addition than a swap.

title: Steam-sensor auto-stop replaces timer
new_elements: Cavity humidity sensor (Detects the steam burst that signals food is hot and stops heating.)
rationale: Only one button needed; the food itself tells the oven when to stop.
judge_comment: Sensor-based auto-stop already exists on many microwaves and is simple, but it is not very radical.

title: Inverter power supply replaces duty-cycle cam
new_elements: Switch-mode inverter magnetron drive (Continuously variable RF output; no HV transformer, doubler cap or diode.)
rationale: Low settings become true gentle heating, so 'defrost' and 'melt' work intuitively without clicking on/off.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves are already on the market, and the user benefit is indirect, so the learning-curve gain is modest.

title: Solid-state RF replaces magnetron
new_elements: GaN solid-state microwave source with closed-loop reflected-power sensing (Low-voltage amplifiers steer energy to the food and stop when absorption drops.); RF power electronics (Semiconductor microwave generation.)
rationale: The oven self-tunes to the food so a single 'heat' press gives even results with no turntable or power choice.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF with closed-loop feedback could enable true one-press operation and is radical, but cost and power levels are still obstacles.

title: Mode-stirrer fan replaces turntable
new_elements: Rotating metal stirrer blade in waveguide (Spreads the field so food sits on a flat fixed floor.)
rationale: No plate to seat correctly, no 'plate too big to turn' problem, nothing to break or wash.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are a long-established alternative to turntables and remove only a minor point of friction, not the learning curve.

title: Rotating antenna under fixed ceramic floor
new_elements: Sub-floor rotating feed antenna (Antenna spins beneath a sealed flat ceramic floor instead of spinning the food.)
rationale: Wipe-clean flat interior; nothing to align or remove.
judge_comment: A spinning antenna under a flat floor is a clever substitution that makes cleaning easier, but it does little for operational simplicity and is harder to engineer than it sounds.

title: Silicone mat replaces glass turntable
new_elements: Food-grade silicone turntable mat with moulded drive lugs (Unbreakable, dishwasher-safe, flexible.)
rationale: Removes the dropped-plate failure and the fiddly re-seating of the glass tray.
judge_comment: A silicone mat is a simple, plausible swap that removes fiddly re-seating, though it is incremental and a flexible mat may sit unevenly with heavy loads.

title: Magnetically coupled turntable drive
new_elements: Through-floor magnetic coupling (Motor under a sealed floor spins a magnet-ring tray; no spindle hole.)
rationale: The tray drops anywhere and self-centres; no coupler to lose or jam.
judge_comment: A magnetic coupling lets the tray be dropped in anywhere with no alignment, which is plausible and directly reduces the learning curve.

title: Pull-out drawer instead of hinged door
new_elements: Sliding drawer cavity with choke on the drawer rim (Pull the handle, food slides out at counter height; push to close and arm.)
rationale: No button to find, no door swinging into the user; the same gesture as a kitchen drawer.
judge_comment: A drawer with a familiar pull-and-push gesture and automatic arming is intuitive, but RF choke sealing on a sliding drawer is challenging.

title: Lift-off glass dome cavity (bell-jar microwave)
new_elements: Mesh-lined glass dome lid with weight-activated interlock (Base plate radiates only when the dome's choke rim is seated and its weight closes the interlocks.)
rationale: Cover it like a cake stand; 360° view and no door logic to learn.
judge_comment: A cake-stand style dome is radically intuitive, but containing microwaves with a glass mesh dome and weight interlocks raises serious safety and engineering concerns.

title: Magnetic soft-latch door without push button
new_elements: Rare-earth magnetic door catch with pull handle (Door holds shut magnetically; pulling the handle opens it and trips the interlocks.)
rationale: Removes the hunt for the release button; every fridge already works this way.
judge_comment: Plausible and familiar fridge-style door, but it only modestly simplifies operation and is not radical; the magnetic latch must also work with safety interlocks.

title: Door pops open as the 'done' signal
new_elements: Solenoid auto-pop door at end of cycle (The door itself opens 5 cm when time runs out, replacing the bell.)
rationale: No ambiguous beep to interpret and food never sits forgotten behind a closed door.
judge_comment: A door that pops open to signal completion is intuitive and needs no learning, and a solenoid actuator is easy to implement, though it could startle users or spill.

title: Foot pedal door opener
new_elements: Bowden-cable foot pedal latch release (Pedal at floor level lifts the door hooks, like a pedal bin.)
rationale: Hands-full users open it with the gesture a bin already taught them.
judge_comment: A foot pedal adds a new control to learn and is awkward for countertop units, so it only helps in niche hands-full cases.

title: Hall-effect sensors replace interlock microswitches
new_elements: Redundant Hall-sensor door detection with relay monitor (Magnets in door, no moving contacts to wear or misalign.)
rationale: Door closes reliably with a light push, so 'why won't it start' moments disappear.
judge_comment: Hall sensors are a sound engineering substitution, but the user benefit for simplicity is indirect and mostly invisible.

title: Conductive elastomer gasket replaces choke seal
new_elements: Compliant RF-conductive silicone door gasket (Metal-loaded elastomer seals RF even with slight door misalignment.)
rationale: The door seals however it is shut, so the user never needs to 'slam it right'.
judge_comment: A forgiving conductive gasket reduces door-closing failures, but RF leakage and durability risks make it harder than claimed, and the benefit is marginal.

title: Fully transparent ITO-coated door, no lamp
new_elements: Transparent conductive oxide RF shield on glass (Replaces perforated metal mesh and the interior lamp with a clear shielded window lit by room light.)
rationale: Unobstructed view of the food means users check progress by looking, not by learning settings.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive RF shield is a real substitution, but it only helps visibility and does little for operation without a learning curve, and shielding at 2.45 GHz while staying clear is hard.

title: Colour-state LED ring replaces bulb and bell
new_elements: Cavity LED ring (amber cooking, green done, red door open) (One light tells state and illuminates food; no separate lamp or bell.)
rationale: Traffic-light colours need no explanation and are visible across the room.
judge_comment: A traffic-light LED ring is cheap, easy to build, and gives intuitive state feedback, though it is an incremental idea.

title: Spoken 'done' chip replaces mechanical bell
new_elements: Voice-sample end-of-cycle announcer (Cheap sound chip says 'your food is ready' in the local language.)
rationale: Nobody has to learn which beep means what.
judge_comment: Voice-sample chips are cheap and common, and a spoken 'done' removes beep ambiguity, but the idea is not radical.

title: Aroma puff as end-of-cycle cue
new_elements: Vent-fan scent cartridge released at cycle end (A food-safe aroma puff from the exhaust signals 'ready' without sound.)
rationale: A silent, instinctive 'something's ready' cue for shared or noise-sensitive spaces.
judge_comment: An aroma cue is highly unusual, but consumable cartridges, food-safety concerns, and ambiguous meaning make it impractical and a weak fit to the need.

title: Cup-shaped pressure pad as the only control
new_elements: Mug-silhouette floor pad that starts a drink program when pressed by a cup (Place the mug on the marked spot and shut the door; nothing else to touch.)
rationale: The student's 90% use case (reheat a drink) becomes a zero-input action.
judge_comment: A mug-sensing pad that needs no controls directly delivers zero-learning operation for the main use case, and weight sensing is feasible, though it only covers drinks.

title: NFC packaging reader replaces control panel
new_elements: NFC/barcode reader in door frame (Ready-meal tag sets time and power automatically.); Near-field communication tags (Passive tags embedded in food packaging.)
rationale: Users stop reading tiny package instructions; the package tells the oven.
judge_comment: Package-driven automation removes all input for tagged meals, but it needs industry adoption and has no fallback for untagged food.

title: Portion-size knob (S/M/L) replaces power knob
new_elements: Three-position portion selector cam (Small/medium/large maps to fixed time-power combinations.)
rationale: Portion size is something everyone can judge; power level is not.
judge_comment: Portion-size mapping is intuitive and easy to build, though it is imprecise across food types and only mildly radical.

title: Single slider from 'warm' to 'boil'
new_elements: Linear slide potentiometer combining time and power (One axis labelled with outcomes, not units.)
rationale: Two knobs collapse into one intuitive 'how hot' gesture.
judge_comment: One outcome-labelled slider is simple and plausible, but combining time and power on one axis limits control.

title: Turn-then-push combo knob
new_elements: Rotary encoder with push-to-start (Turn to a pictogram, push to begin; the only control on the oven.)
rationale: Car-radio familiarity: one knob, two gestures, no hunting.
judge_comment: A single turn-and-push knob with pictograms is very easy to learn and build, but it is close to existing designs.

title: Hand-wave gesture adds 30 seconds
new_elements: IR proximity sensor on fascia (Each wave adds 30 s and starts heating; no knob at all.)
rationale: Greasy hands never touch anything and short reheats are precise.
judge_comment: Wave-to-add-time is hands-free and fun for short reheats, but accidental triggers and a lack of feedback hurt discoverability.

title: Tactile shape-coded knobs replace printed scales
new_elements: Shape- and texture-coded knobs with raised pictograms (Timer is a ridged disc, power a star; readable by touch and in the dark.)
rationale: Removes reading from the task entirely, serving low-vision and first-time users alike.
judge_comment: Directly removes the need to read or learn, highly usable, though tactile knobs are a fairly known concept and only loosely a substitution.

title: Thermostatic 'simmer' duty regulation
new_elements: Cavity-air bimetal duty regulator (A second snap-disc cycles the magnetron based on cavity temperature instead of a timed cam.)
rationale: Power self-adjusts, so the power knob can be deleted.
judge_comment: Auto-regulating power to delete a control is a bold simplification, but cavity-air temperature is a poor proxy for food heating and likely unworkable.

title: PTC self-resetting thermal protection
new_elements: PTC thermistor in-line protector (Solid-state current limiter replaces the snap-disc thermostat.)
rationale: No mysterious 'it stopped working for 10 minutes' thermostat trips to understand.
judge_comment: A PTC protector is plausible and slightly reduces confusion, but it barely affects day-to-day operation.

title: Glazed cavity wall replaces removable mica cover
new_elements: Integrated ceramic-glass waveguide window fused into cavity wall (Non-removable, wipe-clean, cannot be lost or installed wrong.)
rationale: One less part a novice can remove, burn, or forget.
judge_comment: Fusing the waveguide cover removes a misinstallation point, but it is a minor benefit for operation and complicates repair.

title: Self-cleaning ceramic enamel cavity
new_elements: Hydrophobic ceramic-enamel cavity liner (Splatter wipes off with a dry cloth; replaces painted steel.)
rationale: Maintenance becomes a single wipe; no cleaning instructions needed.
judge_comment: Easier cleaning is nice but concerns maintenance rather than operation, and hydrophobic enamel claims are optimistic.

title: Nucleation-etched turntable prevents superheating
new_elements: Glass turntable with micro-etched boiling-stone centre (Surface roughness seeds bubbles so liquids boil visibly instead of erupting.)
rationale: Removes a safety rule the user would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: Plausible safety substitution that removes a hidden rule, but only loosely tied to operating simplicity and not very radical.

title: Metal-detect coil locks out start
new_elements: Inductive metal-detection loop around door frame (Refuses to start and lights a fork icon if metal is detected.)
rationale: The oven enforces the 'no metal' rule so nobody has to remember it.
judge_comment: Inductive metal detection enforces the no-metal rule so nothing needs learning, and it is feasible, though it is an add-on rather than a substitution.

title: Arc-tolerant cavity via reflected-power cut-off
new_elements: Directional coupler arc detector (Kills RF within milliseconds of an arc; metal becomes a harmless mistake.)
rationale: Forgiving hardware replaces user training.
judge_comment: Arc detection via a directional coupler makes metal mistakes harmless and replaces training, though fast arc suppression is hard and the idea is not very simple.

title: Retractable mains cord replaces loose cord
new_elements: Spring-reel retractable power cord (Pull to length, tug to retract, as on a vacuum cleaner.)
rationale: Placement and storage need no cable management.
judge_comment: A feasible retractable cord, but it has little to do with learning-free operation and is not radical.

title: Battery-powered countertop microwave
new_elements: Swappable LiFePO4 pack driving a low-voltage inverter (No mains cord; charge the pack like a power tool.); Low-voltage DC-DC magnetron drive (Boost converter from 48 V battery to magnetron potential.)
rationale: Works anywhere a student lives, with no socket hunting or extension leads.
judge_comment: A battery-powered microwave is bold, but a magnetron draws 1+ kW, which makes it impractical, and it only loosely serves ease of operation.

title: Door-open mechanical capacitor shorting bar
new_elements: Latch-driven HV shorting contact (The door lever physically shorts the HV capacitor every time the door opens.)
rationale: Safety happens through the gesture the user already makes, with no warning labels to read.
judge_comment: A plausible safety mechanism, but it is invisible to the user and does almost nothing for simple operation.

title: Guillotine door that drops shut by gravity
new_elements: Counterweighted vertical sliding door (Lift to open, let go to close; gravity guarantees it latches.)
rationale: Impossible to leave the door ajar, so 'why won't it start' never happens.
judge_comment: A gravity-closing door removes the ajar-door failure, but a vertical door is awkward and has a limited effect on the learning curve.

title: Egg-timer dock replaces built-in timer
new_elements: Universal twist-timer socket on fascia (Any standard kitchen egg timer screws in and its ring-back trips the switch.)
rationale: Users bring the timer they already know how to use.
judge_comment: A familiar twist timer removes the learning curve, though the standardized socket and power switching are awkward.

title: Webcam view replaces lamp and mesh window
new_elements: Cavity camera with front e-paper display (Live image of food on the door, no bulb and no perforated window.)
rationale: A big clear picture of the food is the simplest doneness indicator there is.
judge_comment: A camera and display give an intuitive view of the food, but they are costly and the camera must survive the heat, steam and microwaves.

title: Camera-based doneness auto-stop
new_elements: Low-cost vision model detecting steam, bubbling and melt (Stops heating when the food visually reaches the chosen pictogram state.)
rationale: The user picks 'bubbling' or 'melted' and the oven watches, replacing all timing judgement.
judge_comment: Picking a pictogram and letting the oven watch is very simple to use, but reliable vision-based doneness detection is hard.

title: Electroluminescent cavity liner replaces bulb
new_elements: EL-panel ceiling glow sheet (Flat, shadowless light sheet behind mica; no bulb socket to access or replace.)
rationale: Removes the one serviceable part (bulb) a novice would ever have to deal with.
judge_comment: Bulb replacement is a maintenance point rarely touched by users, so it barely serves simple operation, though it is plausible.

title: Thermochromic door strip shows food heat
new_elements: Thermochromic ink band on cavity floor (Floor changes colour from blue to red as the dish heats; visible through the door.)
rationale: A colour anyone can read replaces guessing from the timer whether the dish is hot.
judge_comment: An intuitive heat indicator helps, but thermochromic ink on a cavity floor would struggle with food heat, washing and durability, and it measures the dish poorly.

title: Single-knob 'minutes only' with fixed full power
new_elements: Deleted power knob; fixed 100% duty cam (Oven only has a timer; defrost is handled by a dedicated 'defrost' detent that pulses via a second cam lobe.)
rationale: Half the controls vanish; most users never touch power anyway.
judge_comment: A timer-only design with a defrost detent is simple, workable and concrete, though not very radical.

title: Weight-indexed timer scale
new_elements: Timer dial printed in grams/portions instead of minutes (Scale reads '1 mug, 1 bowl, 1 plate'; detent positions encode calibrated times.)
rationale: Converts an abstract unit (minutes) into the thing in the user's hand.
judge_comment: A portion-based dial is intuitive and easy to build, but the times depend on food type and wattage, which weakens the calibration.

title: Side-loading rotating cavity drum
new_elements: Half-open rotating drum cavity (Spin the drum to face you to load; spin it back to seal and start, like a revolving door.)
rationale: Loading, sealing and starting become one rotation; no door, button or turntable.
judge_comment: A revolving-door drum merges load, seal and start into one action and is highly radical, but sealing microwave leakage and handling spills in a rotating drum is very hard.

title: Doneness-sensing heat button
new_elements: IR food-surface thermometer (Non-contact IR sensor stops heating when food reaches eating temperature.); Auto-stops when food is hot (Replaces timer setting with a single press.)
rationale: One button and no time guessing removes the whole learning curve of the timer knob.
judge_comment: A single-press IR doneness stop directly removes timer guessing, though IR only reads surface temperature and containers or steam can cause errors.

title: Inverter auto-power
new_elements: Inverter magnetron drive with load sensing (Continuously variable power chosen automatically from reflected RF.)
rationale: The user never chooses a power level because the oven infers it from the load.
judge_comment: Inverter drives already exist, and inferring power from reflected RF is plausible, but the user still has to choose a time, so the learning curve only partly goes away.

title: Mode stirrer replaces turntable
new_elements: Rotating metal mode stirrer in roof (Fan-like paddle scatters RF so food on a flat floor heats evenly.)
rationale: No plate to align or break, so any dish is just put down anywhere.
judge_comment: Mode stirrers are proven and common in commercial ovens, but they have little to do with operation simplicity beyond not needing a plate.

title: Rotating antenna under flat ceramic floor
new_elements: Spinning feed antenna beneath ceramic base (Sweeps the RF pattern instead of moving the food.)
rationale: Flat wipeable floor with no moving dish means nothing to learn about loading.
judge_comment: A rotating antenna under a ceramic floor is feasible and used in some ovens, but it only slightly eases loading and does not touch the controls.

title: Magnetic door seal, no button
new_elements: Magnetic door closure with simple handle (Fridge-style magnet strip holds door; pull to open.)
rationale: Everyone already knows how to open a fridge, so the door needs no instruction.
judge_comment: A fridge-style door is intuitive, but magnetic seals are weak against RF leakage and safety rules, and opening a microwave door is already simple.

title: Hall-effect interlock sensors
new_elements: Redundant Hall-effect magnetic door sensors (Solid-state sensors replace microswitches; no mechanical wear.)
rationale: Reliable door detection means the oven just works every time without fiddling.
judge_comment: Reliable sensing is a sound engineering upgrade, but it does almost nothing for learning curve and is not radical.

title: Self-closing drawer cavity
new_elements: Soft-close drawer cavity (Food placed in a drawer that glides shut and starts automatically.)
rationale: Drawers are universally understood; closing it is the only action required.
judge_comment: A drawer is an intuitive interaction and auto-start removes steps, though it is a big redesign with sealing and RF containment challenges, and it is not really a substitution of a part.

title: Voice announcement instead of bell
new_elements: Speech chip saying 'your food is ready' (Replaces mechanical bell with spoken message.)
rationale: A clear spoken cue needs no interpretation of what the ding means.
judge_comment: A spoken cue is clearer than a beep and is cheap and feasible, but it is a familiar feature and only covers the end of the cycle.

title: Door pops open at end
new_elements: Timer-triggered door spring release (The latch releases itself when the timer runs out, like a toaster.)
rationale: The open door is a self-explanatory signal that the food is done.
judge_comment: The toaster-style pop-open is an intuitive completion signal and is mechanically simple, but it does not simplify the input side and a door springing open could be a nuisance.

title: LED cavity lighting
new_elements: Cool white LED module (Replaces 25 W incandescent lamp; lifetime of appliance.)
rationale: Never needs a bulb change, so there is no hidden maintenance to learn.
judge_comment: LED lighting is a common, sensible swap, but it has little bearing on ease of operation.

title: Electroluminescent cavity walls
new_elements: EL phosphor coating on cavity interior (Walls themselves glow softly when powered.)
rationale: Shadow-free view lets users check food at a glance without any extra control.
judge_comment: Novel glowing walls help visibility but barely address operation simplicity, and EL coating inside a microwave cavity is technically doubtful.

title: Pictogram one-touch buttons
new_elements: Six picture buttons (mug, plate, pizza slice, popcorn, defrost, drink) (Each fixes time and power; no numbers.)
rationale: Pictures replace minutes and watts, so a first-time user succeeds instantly.
judge_comment: Highly effective for zero learning curve and easy to build, but pictogram presets are already common and not radical.

title: Single cold-to-hot slider
new_elements: One linear slider from 'warm' to 'piping hot' (Combines time and power into one intuitive dimension.)
rationale: Replaces two knobs with one that states the outcome, not the mechanism.
judge_comment: A single outcome-based slider is intuitive and simple to implement, though moderately incremental.

title: Weight-sensing auto time
new_elements: Load cell under cavity floor (Weighs food and derives heating time automatically.)
rationale: Put food in, press start; the oven does the arithmetic.
judge_comment: Auto-weighing removes the need to set time, though load cells in a microwave need care and food type still matters.

title: Package barcode reader
new_elements: Barcode/NFC scanner on door frame (Reads ready-meal packaging and applies the printed instructions.)
rationale: Students never read the instructions on the box; the oven reads them instead.
judge_comment: Scanning packaging removes user input for ready meals, but it is limited to packaged food and depends on standardized data.

title: Voice-controlled heating
new_elements: Offline voice command module ('Heat my soup' sets time and power.)
rationale: Natural language is the zero-learning-curve interface.
judge_comment: Voice control is a natural zero-learning interface and is feasible offline, but it is already seen in products and adds parts rather than substituting simpler ones.

title: Steam-sensor auto stop
new_elements: Humidity sensor in exhaust vent (Detects steam burst and ends heating.)
rationale: Removes time setting entirely for most reheating tasks.
judge_comment: Steam-sensing auto stop removes time setting entirely and is proven in sensor-reheat models, though it is not very radical.

title: Food-type dial replaces power knob
new_elements: Dial with soup/plate/frozen/butter icons (Each position maps to an appropriate duty cycle.)
rationale: Users think in foods, not watts.
judge_comment: A food-icon dial is a simple, cheap substitution that matches users' mental models, but it is an incremental idea.

title: Solid-state RF generator
new_elements: GaN solid-state microwave source (Low-voltage transistors replace magnetron, transformer, diode and HV capacitor.)
rationale: Even heating without turntable or power choices means the user just presses go.
judge_comment: A GaN solid-state source is radical and enables even heating and control, but cost and power level remain hurdles and the link to simplicity is indirect.

title: Self-discharging capacitor module
new_elements: Capacitor with integrated bleeder and discharge indicator LED (Visibly shows when safe; no separate resistor.)
rationale: Safety is built in so no warnings need to be learned.
judge_comment: A capacitor with an integrated bleeder is a service safety feature that barely affects user operation or the learning curve.

title: Glazed ceramic cavity, no mica cover
new_elements: Enamelled ceramic waveguide window (Permanent glazed port replaces replaceable mica sheet.)
rationale: No fragile part to burn or replace, so nothing to understand about maintenance.
judge_comment: A permanent glazed port removes a maintenance part but barely affects operating simplicity, and it is not radical.

title: Dishwasher-safe silicone mat floor
new_elements: Removable silicone cavity mat (Replaces glass turntable with unbreakable wipeable mat on flat floor.)
rationale: No plate to seat on a spindle; cleaning is obvious.
judge_comment: A silicone mat removes the plate-seating step, but dropping the turntable hurts heating evenness and silicone could heat or warp, so the benefit to operation is modest.

title: Transparent conductive door film
new_elements: ITO/metal-mesh transparent RF shield (Clear film replaces perforated metal screen.)
rationale: A fully clear window lets users see progress without learning a display.
judge_comment: A transparent conductive film is a plausible, concrete swap, but it only gives visibility and attenuating RF at microwave frequencies is a challenge.

title: Roll-top shutter door
new_elements: Bread-bin style roll-top with conductive slats (Slides up and away; no swing clearance needed.)
rationale: Familiar bread-bin gesture, no button, no door in the way.
judge_comment: A roll-top door is a fresh and intuitive gesture, but sealing RF around moving slats is very hard and it does not simplify the actual cooking controls.

title: Foot-pedal door opener
new_elements: Pedal-actuated door release (Like a kitchen bin; frees the hands.)
rationale: Borrowed from the pedal bin everyone already uses.
judge_comment: A foot pedal is easy to build and familiar, but it adds an unexpected interaction and does little for the learning curve of operating the oven.

title: Proximity auto-open door
new_elements: Capacitive hand-approach sensor (Door opens when a hand with a dish approaches.)
rationale: Zero-touch operation has no instructions to read.
judge_comment: Zero-touch is appealing, but a door that opens on approach is unreliable and a safety concern, and it only covers loading, not setting time or power.

title: Two-position gentle/normal rocker
new_elements: Rocker switch: Gentle / Normal (Replaces 5-step cam with two meaningful choices.)
rationale: Two words instead of five percentages.
judge_comment: A two-word rocker is simple, cheap and easy to build, but it is an incremental simplification rather than a radical one.

title: Food icons on timer dial
new_elements: Timer bezel printed with foods at typical times (Mug at 1:30, plate at 3:00, etc.)
rationale: Guidance is on the knob itself; nothing to memorise.
judge_comment: Food icons at typical times on the dial give guidance exactly where it is needed and cost almost nothing, though the idea is fairly familiar.

title: Sand-glass visual timer
new_elements: Flip hourglass that trips the start switch (Sand level shows remaining time; empty = off.)
rationale: The most universally understood timer there is.
judge_comment: A flip hourglass that trips the start switch is intuitive and playful, but fixed durations and timing accuracy limit it.

title: Colour-strip countdown
new_elements: Shrinking coloured bar replacing numbered dial (Bar length is the time; no digits.)
rationale: Remaining time read instantly from across the room.
judge_comment: A shrinking colour bar is readable from across the room and needs no digits, but it is less precise and the mechanism is vague.

title: Thermal fuse replaces thermostat
new_elements: One-shot thermal fuse plus PTC current limiter (Fewer moving parts, fails safe.)
rationale: Invisible safety with no reset behaviour for the user to learn.
judge_comment: Plausible, safe substitution, but invisible to the user and barely affects ease of operation; a one-shot fuse also means service burden.

title: Airflow-driven turntable
new_elements: Turbine turntable spun by cooling-fan exhaust (Removes the separate turntable motor.)
rationale: Fewer parts, same even heating, nothing new to operate.
judge_comment: Clever parts reduction, but it does little for the no-learning-curve need and airflow-driven rotation may be inconsistent.

title: Battery-powered dorm microwave
new_elements: Removable Li-ion pack (300 Wh) (Replaces mains cord for a few heating sessions.)
rationale: Works anywhere with no socket hunting or cable management.
judge_comment: Portability is convenient, but a 300 Wh pack can't deliver typical 1 kW microwave power for long, and it adds charging to manage.

title: Conductive gasket door seal
new_elements: Compressible metal-mesh gasket (Replaces precision quarter-wave choke rim.)
rationale: Door seals even if slammed carelessly, forgiving of untrained use.
judge_comment: A forgiving door seal helps careless use and is a concrete substitution, though mesh gaskets wear and leak over time.

title: RF-absorbing curtain doorless oven
new_elements: Hanging RF-absorbent ferrite-loaded curtain (Walk-through access with no door or latch.)
rationale: Nothing to open or close at all.
judge_comment: Radically removes the door interaction, but safely containing microwave leakage with an open curtain is essentially unrealistic.

title: Microwave pot with lid
new_elements: Pot-shaped cavity with lift-off lid containing the interlock (Looks and works like a saucepan.)
rationale: Cooking metaphor everyone understands: lid on, heat; lid off, stop.
judge_comment: A pot-shaped cavity with a lid-interlock uses a familiar cooking metaphor, but it is limited in capacity and still needs some way to set time or power.

title: Hold-to-heat dead-man button
new_elements: Momentary heat button (Heats only while pressed, like a tap.)
rationale: Direct cause-and-effect control with nothing to set.
judge_comment: A hold-to-heat button is very simple and technically trivial, with no settings to learn, though it is tiring for longer cooking times.

title: Falling-weight clockwork timer
new_elements: Visible weight-driven timer with chain (Pull the chain to set; weight drops to zero.)
rationale: Time left is visible as height, intuitive for anyone.
judge_comment: A visible weight-and-chain mechanical timer is intuitive and cheap, and it is a genuine substitution for the electronic timer, though it is bulky and imprecise.

title: Scent-release done signal
new_elements: Aroma puff cartridge triggered at end (Pleasant smell replaces the bell.)
rationale: A non-intrusive cue understood without instruction.
judge_comment: A scent cartridge is novel, but consumables, ambiguity and the odor of the food itself make it a weak fit for a simple, no-learning-curve signal.

title: Thermochromic door glass
new_elements: Thermochromic laminate on door window (Window tints red as food gets hot.)
rationale: Colour tells users 'hot' with no display or lamp.
judge_comment: Thermochromic glass gives an intuitive hot signal, but door-window temperature will not reliably track food temperature and the laminate would struggle in a microwave environment.

title: Thermal-image projection on door
new_elements: Low-res thermal camera projecting heat map on door (Shows cold spots so users stir only if needed.)
rationale: Visual truth replaces guesswork about doneness.
