new_elements: Linear slide timer with plate silhouettes (Horizontal slider marked with cup, bowl, small plate, large plate silhouettes; slider creeps back to zero.); Rack-and-pinion clockwork slider (Slider rack drives the same synchronous timer motor.)
rationale: Matching a slider to the physical size of what you are heating is a direct, number-free mapping.
judge_comment: A number-free slider mapped to the physical size of the load is intuitive and mechanically plausible, though size is a rough proxy for heating time.

title: Press-per-minute counter button
new_elements: Ratchet 'add a minute' button (Each press mechanically advances the timer cam 60 s; a window shows filled dots; press with a bump for 30 s.); Ratchet-indexed cam advance (Pawl advances timer shaft by fixed angle per press.)
rationale: Counting presses is simpler than reading a dial and makes short durations exact.
judge_comment: A press-to-add-minute ratchet is simple and easy to build, but it is similar to existing +30 s buttons and offers little novelty.

title: Door handle rotation sets the time
new_elements: Rotary door handle timer (Closing the door, you twist the handle like a tap; twist angle sets minutes and the handle slowly un-twists to vertical when done.); Handle-shaft coupled clockwork (Handle shaft mates with timer shaft through the door frame when closed.)
rationale: Closing and setting become one gesture on one part, with no separate panel to understand.
judge_comment: Merging door closing and time-setting into one gesture is very intuitive, but mechanically coupling a handle to a timer through the door frame is tricky and has safety-interlock implications.

title: Pop-up probe thermometer replaces the timer
new_elements: Bimetal pop-up food probe with cavity switch (A turkey-style pop-up probe stuck into food; when it pops it releases a lever that trips the mains switch via a thin tether.); Bimetal pop-up thermometer (Spring held by solder/bimetal releases at set temperature.)
rationale: Heat until it pops is a familiar roast-turkey cue that replaces guessing minutes.
judge_comment: A familiar cue, but a metal probe in a microwave risks arcing, the mechanical tether is awkward, and users still need to know how to start and set up the probe.

title: Colour-gradient dial (blue to red) instead of numbers
new_elements: Blue-to-red continuous colour knob (Power knob face is a colour gradient with snowflake and flame ends; no numeric levels.); In-mould decorated gradient overlay (Printed film insert-moulded on the knob.)
rationale: Colour temperature metaphors are understood cross-culturally and need no manual.
judge_comment: An easy-to-build, intuitive knob, but it only addresses power, not time, and the lack of numbers reduces precision.

title: Flashing lamp + door unlatch replaces the bell
new_elements: Blinking cavity LED end signal (At cycle end the cavity LED flashes slowly until the door opens, giving a silent, persistent cue; bell deleted.); Astable LED flasher (Two-transistor blink circuit triggered by timer end contact.)
rationale: A visual that persists until acted upon is more forgiving for distracted or hard-of-hearing users than a one-shot ding.
judge_comment: A simple, feasible substitution that helps accessibility, but it does little to cut the learning curve and is not radical.

title: Hand-wave proximity door opener
new_elements: IR proximity sensor + solenoid latch (Wave a hand in front of the door and a solenoid pops it open; no button to find.); Reflective IR proximity detection (IR LED/phototransistor pair as in automatic soap dispensers.)
rationale: Borrowing the automatic-door gesture people already use in public restrooms eliminates search for the release.
judge_comment: Plausible with off-the-shelf parts, but it risks accidental triggering, and opening the door is a minor part of operating a microwave.

title: Plate-slot microwave (insert like toast)
new_elements: Vertical plate slot with spring platform (A slim vertical slot: slide a dinner plate in edge-first; a self-closing choke flap seals, a mode stirrer evens the field.); Self-sealing slot choke flap (Gravity flap with quarter-wave lips around a narrow slot opening.)
rationale: Loading becomes a single slide motion with no door, button or tray alignment.
judge_comment: A very radical, intuitive loading action, but a spring-loaded choke slot that must contain microwave leakage and handle liquids is a major engineering challenge.

title: Two-position rocker: 'a little' / 'a lot'
new_elements: Little/Lot rocker switch (Rocker left = 40 s at 50 %, right = 2.5 min at 100 %; spring returns to centre when the clockwork expires.); Dual-preset clockwork with rocker trigger (Two fixed cam tracks selected by rocker direction.)
rationale: A binary choice described in plain words is the lowest possible cognitive load.
judge_comment: Very simple and clearly feasible with a mechanical clockwork, though it is more an incremental simplification than a radical idea.

title: Smart container with passive resonator stops the oven
new_elements: Temperature-detuning resonator container lid (Included container lid carries a passive split-ring resonator whose resonance shifts at 70 °C; a cavity pickup senses the shift and ends the cycle.); Thermally detuned passive RF resonator sensing (Thermo-responsive dielectric shifts resonance read by a cavity antenna.)
rationale: Put food in the box, put the box in, press go: the container closes the loop so no timing knowledge is required.
judge_comment: A clever passive resonator that closes the loop, but it requires a special container and tricky RF sensing, and it adds complexity rather than substituting something simpler.

title: Defrost cloche replaces the power knob
new_elements: Perforated metal 'gentle' cloche (A mesh dome placed over frozen or delicate food attenuates the field to ~30 %; the oven runs at one power only.); Mesh-dome partial RF shielding (Hole pattern sized for ~5 dB attenuation while avoiding arcing via rounded edges.)
rationale: Covering delicate food is intuitive kitchen behaviour, so power selection disappears as a concept.
judge_comment: Substituting a physical cover for a power setting is intuitive, but the attenuation is hard to control and mesh in a microwave raises arcing and uneven heating concerns.

title: Hourglass-style visible countdown replaces dial
new_elements: Rotating transparent sand timer cartridge (Flip the visible sand timer (1, 2 or 5 min cartridges); an optical gate detects empty top bulb and cuts power.); Optical gate sand-level detection (LED/phototransistor beam across the upper bulb.)
rationale: An hourglass is self-explanatory and shows remaining time physically to anyone at any age.
judge_comment: An intuitive and feasible hourglass timer, though fixed cartridges limit flexibility and the optical sensing adds components.

title: Dinner-plate recess instead of turntable
new_elements: Moulded plate-shaped cavity floor recess (Fixed glass-ceramic floor with a shallow dish-shaped recess that self-centres plates and catches spills; combined with mode stirring.); Formed glass-ceramic floor (Pressed glass-ceramic panel with integral spill lip.)
rationale: The floor tells you where the plate goes and there is nothing to lift out, lose or re-seat.
judge_comment: A plausible turntable-free design that makes plate placement obvious, but the gain in operational simplicity is modest and uneven heating is a risk.

title: Inverter supply with 'Gentle/Fast' toggle
new_elements: Switch-mode inverter HV supply + two-way toggle (High-frequency inverter continuously varies magnetron power; a plain toggle gives 30 % or 100 %.); Resonant inverter HV power supply (Ferrite transformer at ~30 kHz with closed-loop current control.)
rationale: Real continuous power means 'gentle' actually defrosts without cycling confusion, so one toggle suffices.
judge_comment: Inverter supplies already exist and a two-position toggle is very simple, though it is not a radical substitution.

title: Weight-sensitive power: light loads automatically get gentle power
new_elements: Load-cell floor driving duty-cycle cam (A spring floor plate shifts the power cam: under 150 g (butter, chocolate) runs at 30 %, heavier loads at full.); Mass-proportional cam offset (Floor deflection lever repositions the duty-cycle cam follower.)
rationale: Small delicate items are protected automatically, so the user never has to know what 'power level 2' means.
judge_comment: Weight-based automatic power removes the need to understand power levels, but a mechanical load-cell cam is imprecise and the 150 g threshold is crude.

title: Window-shutter cavity: open front, no door
new_elements: Motorised roll-up metal shutter front (A corrugated conductive shutter rolls up when idle so the cavity is a shelf; pressing start rolls it down into a choke track and heats.); Conductive tambour with continuous choke track (Interlocking metal slats seated in a quarter-wave channel.)
rationale: No door to open: place food on an open shelf and press one button, removing the door-handling step entirely.
judge_comment: Very radical, but a roll-up shutter with an RF choke raises serious leakage and safety problems and the door was not a real usability barrier.

title: Fridge-magnet style recipe cards slot into the fascia
new_elements: Keyed program card slot (Rigid cards (soup, rice, popcorn, defrost) with punched edge notches slide into the fascia and mechanically set cam positions.); Punched-card mechanical programming (Card notches position follower levers for time and power.)
rationale: Choosing a picture card is a recognition task, not a recall-and-configure task.
judge_comment: Picture-based punched cards replace recall with recognition and are mechanically feasible, though they add loose parts to manage.

title: Scent-free 'steam whistle' replaces bell
new_elements: Exhaust-air whistle vent (Timer end diverts fan airflow through a reed whistle for 5 s then the fan stops; kettle-like cue, no striker or bell.); Air-driven reed whistle (Flap valve routes exhaust through a tuned reed.)
rationale: A kettle whistle is an established 'food is hot' signal people respond to instinctively.
judge_comment: A familiar kettle-whistle cue is intuitive and removes the bell, but it adds a flap valve and reed and may be noisy or unreliable at the end of a cycle, and it only mildly improves operation simplicity.

title: Fixed-brightness LED window strip replaces 25 W lamp and lamp door
new_elements: Edge-lit LED door window (LEDs in the door frame edge-light the inner glass pane, illuminating the cavity from the front with no bulb inside and no access panel.); Edge-lit light guide panel (LEDs couple into a glass pane with micro-etched extraction features.)
rationale: Lifetime lighting removes the one maintenance task a novice would otherwise have to learn.
judge_comment: Edge-lit glass panel is a plausible way to remove the bulb, but it has little to do with learning-free operation and a microwave door pane needs a metal mesh and RF shielding, which complicates the design.
